record.scope: New application, unchanged complete native/build inputs and retained original binary/receipts. This is input equivalence, not a build at the new application commit and not inherited gameplay qualification.

scope: Existing cumulative native stage readback only; no simulation/worker/render treatment. All original frozenV3 physical gates remain required. Stage brackets measure elapsed wall time, including waits/descheduling. The remainder is native tick elapsed outside sequential Wave brackets, not proven non-Water CPU. No native start, GPU, scanout or owner acceptance claim.

process.memory_scope: 250ms actual Godot process working-set/RSS samples including setup and capture; valid only after receipt PID match. Windows virtual size unavailable; commit reported separately.

summary.scope: Actual owned Godot process CPU accounting, all its threads. Includes scene setup and capture inside the sampled process lifetime. Samples are not aligned to Godot capture clocks. The unobserved launch/exit tail is excluded from interval deltas; last cumulative counters are lower bounds on lifetime CPU. Read time for successful and failed queries is external sampler wall cost, not Godot CPU; elapsed_ms marks query request, not an instantaneous kernel accounting timestamp. No GPU busy-time or hardware utilization claim.

same_frame_continuation.scope: Observed actual callback and immutable owner receipts; no modeled or extrapolated speedup.

first_10s.physical_boundary_scope: Observed window boundaries, including censored no-step prefixes/suffixes; separate from between-completion gap distributions.
first_10s.first_ready_scope: First healthy matching world/native-tick/body-sample/terrain packet. Observation clock is full snapshot hook exit (queue lower bound); exact physics handoff remains unavailable on accepted main. Latest handoff metrics above remain separately reported.
first_10s.draw_clock_scope: Next delivered frame_post_draw callback only; no upload-specific draw identity, GPU completion or scanout assertion, especially under Separate rendering.

gpu_history.scope: current GPU against source CPU; prior plane hash retained; transition oracle separately verifies both histories

observation_limits: Native completion common clock is existing post-tick result-capture entry; exact legacy completion timestamp is unavailable.
frame_post_draw is callback delivery, not hardware GPU completion or scanout.
Final gameplay state endpoints may have different tick counts; only first-144-step trajectories have equal physical-step endpoints.
Current GPU bytes are compared with source CPU bytes. Both-plane history parity is a separate retained transition oracle.
This fixed actor-input test does not replace human contact, painting, camera movement, authoring, save/reopen or physical Windows/NVIDIA acceptance.
Every actual command attempt and admission is recorded; repeated callbacks preserve historical input refresh, so admitted command counts can differ by source cadence.
Once-per-step is a separately labelled diagnostic requiring equal-step body and admitted-move parity before use. Six-tick input leases expire by completed physical ticks, not wall time.
Render owner must match safe/separate in every arm. Next delivered frame_post_draw callback is not an upload-specific draw receipt.
Reduced-observer calibration disables detailed Main/worker traces and participation sampling; the completed-step/body and command oracle remains. It is not an uninstrumented owner run.
The historical Wave cohort explicitly requests one round, core reference parameters, no spill and no ballistic transport. Current owner gameplay Wave defaults are a separate workload.
Same-frame continuation is at most one nonblocking attempt within the latest withheld genuine physics callback's original process frame. It does not create a callback or carry physics time credit.
V3 observer records genuine callback ownership and continuation attempts. Its reduced observer retains that proof and cannot reuse the v2 observer calibration as an overhead bound.

Source C primary explicitly enables the experiment. Ordinary application and owner launcher defaults remain OFF. C-only OFF/ON/ON/OFF is the causal control; M/I/C timings alone are whole-source comparisons.

Separate full-Workbench controls are retired from this prospective Safe-only campaign after the original engine startup/crash failures. Their v2 registration and every negative receipt remain frozen; native-independent renderer probes separately investigate the failure.

material_steps_policy.scope: Exact committed/staged Main and helper plus actual pre/post request/status; absent legacy capability is distinct from implemented effective0.

execution_derivation.scope: Only additive same-iteration CPU reads and a bounded sidecar; all frozen process ownership and completion gates remain exact.

bundle.scope: Explicit supplementary Main presentation and whole-process CPU observations; frozen physical gates and production defaults unchanged.

presentation.scope: Actual Main submitted overlay state at pre-draw. The first visible part is joined to the real roster node/RID and actual collider-local transform; compound composition uses a float32 roundoff bound including absolute operand magnitudes under cancellation. Additional parts are not individually checked. Unsupported geometry and pre-capture physical poses remain explicitly unverified. Withholding, pose age and Follow lag are submitted-state observations, not scanout, display refresh or input-device latency. Separate draw notifications remain unassociated.

cpu.scope: Actual owned Godot process CPU accounting, all its threads. Includes scene setup and capture inside the sampled process lifetime. Samples are not aligned to Godot capture clocks. The unobserved launch/exit tail is excluded from interval deltas; last cumulative counters are lower bounds on lifetime CPU. Read time for successful and failed queries is external sampler wall cost, not Godot CPU; elapsed_ms marks query request, not an instantaneous kernel accounting timestamp. No GPU busy-time or hardware utilization claim.

observers.scope: Additional submitted-pose and whole-process CPU evidence. Disabled pose/freshness is unavailable, never zero; actual displayed pixels and input-device latency remain unobserved.
